blocks.content: Soil is a dynamic natural body composed of mineral and organic constituents, living organisms, air, and water.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Soil functions as a dynamic natural system involving continuous biological, physical, and chemical transformations.
A balanced soil composition consists of 45% mineral matter, 5% organic matter, 25% air, and 25% water by volume.
Soil science is divided into two main branches: Pedology (origin and morphology) and Edaphology (relation to plant growth).
Soil formation (pedogenesis) is controlled by active factors (Climate, Organisms) and passive factors (Parent Material, Relief, Time).

rows: Study of soil as a natural body, origin, and classification
Study of soil properties in relation to plant growth and yield
Understanding soil formation, morphology, and mapping
Optimizing soil fertility, nutrient availability, and agricultural productivity

items: Soil air has a higher concentration of Carbon Dioxide (0.3% to 1%) compared to atmospheric air (0.04%) due to root and microbial respiration.
Questions frequently test active soil-forming factors (Climate, Organisms/Biota) versus passive factors (Relief/Topography, Parent Material, Time).
Understand the key difference between Pedology (soil as a natural body) and Edaphology (soil in relation to agriculture and crop yield).
